    pub physical_size: [UVec2](https://docs.rs/glam/0.32.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/glam/u32/uvec2/struct.UVec2.html),
    pub logical_size: [UVec2](https://docs.rs/glam/0.32.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/glam/u32/uvec2/struct.UVec2.html),
    pub window_mode: [WindowMode](https://docs.rs/bevy_window/0.19.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bevy_window/window/enum.WindowMode.html),
    pub monitor_index: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
}## Expand description

Event fired when a window restore completes and the window becomes visible.

This is an [ EntityEvent](https://docs.rs/bevy_ecs/0.19.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bevy_ecs/event/trait.EntityEvent.html) triggered on the window entity at the end of the restore
process, after position, size, and window mode have been applied. Dependent crates can
observe this event to know the final restored window state.

Use an observer to receive this event:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// For all windows
app.add_observer(|trigger: On<WindowRestored>| {
    let event = trigger.event();
    // Use `event.entity`, `event.physical_size`, `event.window_mode`, etc.
});
// For primary window only - check event.entity against PrimaryWindow query
fn on_window_restored(
    trigger: On<WindowRestored>,
    primary_window: Query<(), With<PrimaryWindow>>,
) {
    let event = trigger.event();
    if primary_window.get(event.entity).is_ok() {
        // Handle primary window only
    }
}
```

# ManagedWindowPersistence in bevy_clerestory - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bevy_clerestory/0.1.1/bevy_clerestory/enum.ManagedWindowPersistence.html

```
pub enum ManagedWindowPersistence {
    RememberAll,
    ActiveOnly,
}
```
## Expand description

Controls what happens to saved state when a managed window is despawned.

Set as a resource on the app to control persistence behavior for all windows.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.RememberAll)

### RememberAll

Default: saved state persists even if window is closed during the session. All windows ever opened are remembered in the state file.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ActiveOnly)

### ActiveOnly

Only windows open at time of save are persisted. Closing a window removes its entry from the state file.

# Platform in bevy_clerestory - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bevy_clerestory/0.1.1/bevy_clerestory/enum.Platform.html

```
pub enum Platform {
    MacOs,
    Windows,
    X11,
    Wayland,
}
```
## Expand description

The display platform, detected once at startup and inserted as a [ Resource](https://docs.rs/bevy_ecs/0.19.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bevy_ecs/resource/trait.Resource.html).

All platform-specific window restoration behavior is expressed as methods on
this enum rather than ad-hoc `cfg!()` / `is_wayland()` checks.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MacOs)

### MacOs

macOS.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Windows)

### Windows

Windows.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.X11)

### X11

Linux running an X11 session.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Wayland)

### Wayland

Linux running a Wayland session.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Detect the current platform.

On Linux, checks `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` to distinguish Wayland from X11.
On macOS and Windows the result is compile-time constant.

#### pub const fn [position_available](https://docs.rs#method.position_available)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Whether window position is available from the windowing system.

Wayland does not expose window position to clients (`wl_surface` has no
position API, and winit returns `(0, 0)`). All other platforms provide it.

Whether the given target and actual window modes should be considered a match during settle comparison.

On Wayland, exclusive fullscreen is not supported by winit and falls back to borderless fullscreen. The settle system must accept this substitution.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bevy_clerestory/platform.rs.html#113-123)#### pub const fn [should_hide_on_startup](https://docs.rs#method.should_hide_on_startup)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

#### pub const fn [should_hide_on_startup](https://docs.rs#method.should_hide_on_startup)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Whether the primary window should be hidden on startup to prevent a flash at the default position before restore completes.

On Linux X11 with frame extent compensation (`workaround-winit-4445`),
the window must stay visible so `_NET_FRAME_EXTENTS` can be queried.
All other platforms hide the window.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bevy_clerestory/platform.rs.html#130-139)#### pub const fn [needs_frame_compensation](https://docs.rs#method.needs_frame_compensation)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bevy_clerestory/platform.rs.html#130-139)

#### pub const fn [needs_frame_compensation](https://docs.rs#method.needs_frame_compensation)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Whether X11 frame extent compensation is needed.

Only applies to Linux X11 with the `workaround-winit-4445` feature,
where `outer_position()` is offset by the title bar height.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bevy_clerestory/platform.rs.html#149)#### pub const fn [position_reliable_for_settle](https://docs.rs#method.position_reliable_for_settle)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bevy_clerestory/platform.rs.html#149)

#### pub const fn [position_reliable_for_settle](https://docs.rs#method.position_reliable_for_settle)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Whether position readback is reliable for settle comparison.

On X11 with `workaround-winit-4445`, the target position is in frame
coordinates (compensated by `frame_top`), but `Window.position` reports
the client area position (the W6 bug). The two reference frames differ
by exactly the title bar height, so position comparison always fails.
Other platforms have consistent position readback.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bevy_clerestory/platform.rs.html#157)#### pub const fn [should_clamp_position](https://docs.rs#method.should_clamp_position)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bevy_clerestory/platform.rs.html#157)

#### pub const fn [should_clamp_position](https://docs.rs#method.should_clamp_position)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Whether saved position should be clamped to monitor bounds.

macOS clamps because it may resize/reposition windows that extend beyond the screen and does not allow windows to span monitors. All other platforms preserve the exact saved position.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bevy_clerestory/platform.rs.html#164)#### pub const fn [exclusive_fullscreen_fallback](https://docs.rs#method.exclusive_fullscreen_fallback)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bevy_clerestory/platform.rs.html#164)

#### pub const fn [exclusive_fullscreen_fallback](https://docs.rs#method.exclusive_fullscreen_fallback)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Whether exclusive fullscreen should fall back to borderless.

On Wayland, winit ignores exclusive fullscreen requests, so the library restores as borderless fullscreen instead.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bevy_clerestory/platform.rs.html#242-244)#### pub const fn [needs_managed_scale_fixup](https://docs.rs#method.needs_managed_scale_fixup)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bevy_clerestory/platform.rs.html#242-244)

#### pub const fn [needs_managed_scale_fixup](https://docs.rs#method.needs_managed_scale_fixup)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Whether managed windows need scale strategy recalculation on creation.

A managed (secondary) window is created on the monitor where the focused
window currently is, not necessarily the monitor whose scale was sampled
when its `TargetPosition` was computed:

- **Windows**: new windows may be placed on the OS primary display rather than the monitor where the parent/launching window is.
- **macOS / X11**: the primary window migrates to its own restore target during startup, so a secondary window spawned alongside it is born on the primary’s post-move monitor — a different scale than the primary’s launch monitor that- `restore_managed_window`sampled for- `starting_scale`.

In all three cases the `starting_scale` assumption is wrong, so `restore_windows`
re-reads the window’s actual `base_scale_factor()` and recomputes the strategy.

Enabled for every non-Wayland platform. The recompute only runs when the
measured scale differs from `starting_scale`, so on setups where all
monitors share one scale factor (the common X11 case, where winit derives
a single global scale from `Xft.dpi`) the branch is unreachable and this is
a no-op. Wayland is excluded: it handles DPI natively and exposes no window
position, so the cross-DPI strategies never apply there.

# Resource in bevy_ecs::resource - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bevy_ecs/0.19.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bevy_ecs/resource/trait.Resource.html

`pub trait Resource: `[Component](https://docs.rs/component/trait.Component.html) { }## Expand description

A type that can be inserted into a [ World](https://docs.rs/world/struct.World.html) as a singleton.

You can access resource data in systems using the [ Res](https://docs.rs/change_detection/struct.Res.html) and

[system parameters](https://docs.rs/change_detection/struct.ResMut.html)

`ResMut`Only one resource of each type can be stored in a [ World](https://docs.rs/world/struct.World.html) at any given time.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
#[derive(Resource)]
struct MyResource { value: u32 }
world.insert_resource(MyResource { value: 42 });
fn read_resource_system(resource: Res<MyResource>) {
    assert_eq!(resource.value, 42);
}
fn write_resource_system(mut resource: ResMut<MyResource>) {
    assert_eq!(resource.value, 42);
    resource.value = 0;
    assert_eq!(resource.value, 0);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#sync-resources)`!Sync` Resources

A `!Sync` type cannot implement `Resource`. However, it is possible to wrap a `Send` but not `Sync`
type in [ SyncCell](https://docs.rs/bevy_platform/0.19.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bevy_platform/cell/sync_cell/struct.SyncCell.html) or the currently unstable

[to make it](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/sync/struct.Exclusive.html)

`Exclusive``Sync`. This forces only
having mutable access (`&mut T` only, never `&T`), but makes it safe to reference across multiple
threads.This will fail to compile since `RefCell` is `!Sync`.

This will compile since the `RefCell` is wrapped with `SyncCell`.

```
use bevy_platform::cell::SyncCell;
#[derive(Resource)]
struct ActuallySync {
   counter: SyncCell<RefCell<usize>>,
}
```
## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# car-reason

Code reasoning engine for [Common Agent Runtime](https://github.com/Parslee-ai/car). Adaptive, graph-driven, learning.

## What it does

Instead of a hardcoded "diagnose → suggest → explain" pipeline, reasoning actions are **skills in the memgine graph**. The graph's spreading activation and success/failure tracking determine which actions to run, in what order, routed to which models. As outcomes accumulate, the routing improves without code changes.

## Usage

```
use ;
use ReasoningSession;
let inference = new;
let mut memgine = new;
// Seed the default reasoning skills
seed_defaults;
let memgine = new;
let session = new;
let result = session.reason.await?;
println!;
for s in &result.suggestions
println!;
```
## Where it fits

A higher-level capability over `car-memgine` + `car-inference` + `car-ast`. Used by the `car` CLI's diagnostic / fix slash commands and by `.claude-plugin/agents/reason.md`.

## Inference handle abstraction (Parslee-ai/car#189)

`ReasoningSession` does not depend on the concrete `InferenceEngine`. It holds an `Arc<dyn ReasoningInferenceHandle>` — the narrow trait surface this crate exports in [ handle.rs](https://docs.rs/src/handle.rs).

The trait extends [ car_inference::InferenceHandle](https://docs.rs/car-inference/src/handle.rs) (which provides

`generate` + `embed`) with three reasoning-specific methods:| Method | Used for | In-process impl | Daemon impl |
|---|---|---|---|
| `generate_tracked(req)` | Per-action `InferenceResult`(trace_id, model_used, latency_ms) | `InferenceEngine::generate_tracked` | daemon's `infer`JSON-RPC method |
| `find_model_by_name(name)` | Tier-picker checks whether a candidate model is registered before naming it | `unified_registry.find_by_name` | cached `models.list_unified`snapshot |
| `record_inferred_outcomes(action_results)` | Post-session learning loop (writes inferred outcomes for each action's trace) | takes the engine's tracker write lock | best-effort no-op (no `outcomes.resolve_pending`endpoint yet — follow-up) |

This lets callers pick the inference backend at runtime:

```
// In-process (offline dev, tests, CI)
let inference:  =
    new;
// Daemon-routed (`car-server` running locally; shared hot weights + accumulated profiles)
let inference:  =
    new;
```
`cmd_reason` in `car-cli` does the runtime selection — probes the daemon with a cheap `models.list` RPC and falls back to an embedded engine if unreachable. See `car-rs/crates/car-cli/src/daemon_handle.rs` for the daemon-side `ReasoningInferenceHandle` impl.

**Why a new trait instead of growing  InferenceHandle.**

`InferenceHandle` (added in #188 for memgine) is intentionally minimal — `generate` + `embed` — because memgine is reachable from many crates and a wide trait surface multiplies daemon-proxy work for every implementor. `ReasoningInferenceHandle` extends it with the three methods car-reason actually uses, keeping the lower-level trait clean while still letting daemon impls compose: `DaemonInferenceHandle` implements both, with one shared WebSocket connection.

---

seed_defaults;
let memgine = new;
let session = new;
let result = session.reason.await?;
println!;
for s in &result.suggestions
println!;
```
## Where it fits

A higher-level capability over `car-memgine` + `car-inference` + `car-ast`. Used by the `car` CLI's diagnostic / fix slash commands and by `.claude-plugin/agents/reason.md`.

## Inference handle abstraction (Parslee-ai/car#189)

`ReasoningSession` does not depend on the concrete `InferenceEngine`. It holds an `Arc<dyn ReasoningInferenceHandle>` — the narrow trait surface this crate exports in [ handle.rs](https://docs.rs/src/handle.rs).

The trait extends [ car_inference::InferenceHandle](https://docs.rs/car-inference/src/handle.rs) (which provides

`generate` + `embed`) with three reasoning-specific methods:| Method | Used for | In-process impl | Daemon impl |
|---|---|---|---|
| `generate_tracked(req)` | Per-action `InferenceResult`(trace_id, model_used, latency_ms) | `InferenceEngine::generate_tracked` | daemon's `infer`JSON-RPC method |
| `find_model_by_name(name)` | Tier-picker checks whether a candidate model is registered before naming it | `unified_registry.find_by_name` | cached `models.list_unified`snapshot |
| `record_inferred_outcomes(action_results)` | Post-session learning loop (writes inferred outcomes for each action's trace) | takes the engine's tracker write lock | best-effort no-op (no `outcomes.resolve_pending`endpoint yet — follow-up) |

This lets callers pick the inference backend at runtime:

```
// In-process (offline dev, tests, CI)
let inference:  =
    new;
// Daemon-routed (`car-server` running locally; shared hot weights + accumulated profiles)
let inference:  =
    new;
```
`cmd_reason` in `car-cli` does the runtime selection — probes the daemon with a cheap `models.list` RPC and falls back to an embedded engine if unreachable. See `car-rs/crates/car-cli/src/daemon_handle.rs` for the daemon-side `ReasoningInferenceHandle` impl.

**Why a new trait instead of growing  InferenceHandle.**

`InferenceHandle` (added in #188 for memgine) is intentionally minimal — `generate` + `embed` — because memgine is reachable from many crates and a wide trait surface multiplies daemon-proxy work for every implementor. `ReasoningInferenceHandle` extends it with the three methods car-reason actually uses, keeping the lower-level trait clean while still letting daemon impls compose: `DaemonInferenceHandle` implements both, with one shared WebSocket connection.

---

`InferenceHandle` (added in #188 for memgine) is intentionally minimal — `generate` + `embed` — because memgine is reachable from many crates and a wide trait surface multiplies daemon-proxy work for every implementor. `ReasoningInferenceHandle` extends it with the three methods car-reason actually uses, keeping the lower-level trait clean while still letting daemon impls compose: `DaemonInferenceHandle` implements both, with one shared WebSocket connection.

---

# car-reason 0.9.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/car-reason/0.9.0

# car-reason

Code reasoning engine for [Common Agent Runtime](https://github.com/Parslee-ai/car). Adaptive, graph-driven, learning.

## What it does

Instead of a hardcoded "diagnose → suggest → explain" pipeline, reasoning actions are **skills in the memgine graph**. The graph's spreading activation and success/failure tracking determine which actions to run, in what order, routed to which models. As outcomes accumulate, the routing improves without code changes.

## Usage

```
use ;
use ReasoningSession;
let inference = new;
let mut memgine = new;
// Seed the default reasoning skills
seed_defaults;
let memgine = new;
let session = new;
let result = session.reason.await?;
println!;
for s in &result.suggestions
println!;
```
## Where it fits

A higher-level capability over `car-memgine` + `car-inference` + `car-ast`. Used by the `car` CLI's diagnostic / fix slash commands and by `.claude-plugin/agents/reason.md`.

## Inference handle abstraction (Parslee-ai/car#189)

`ReasoningSession` does not depend on the concrete `InferenceEngine`. It holds an `Arc<dyn ReasoningInferenceHandle>` — the narrow trait surface this crate exports in [ handle.rs](https://docs.rs/src/handle.rs).

The trait extends [ car_inference::InferenceHandle](https://docs.rs/car-inference/src/handle.rs) (which provides

`generate` + `embed`) with three reasoning-specific methods:| Method | Used for | In-process impl | Daemon impl |
|---|---|---|---|
| `generate_tracked(req)` | Per-action `InferenceResult`(trace_id, model_used, latency_ms) | `InferenceEngine::generate_tracked` | daemon's `infer`JSON-RPC method |
| `find_model_by_name(name)` | Tier-picker checks whether a candidate model is registered before naming it | `unified_registry.find_by_name` | cached `models.list_unified`snapshot |
| `record_inferred_outcomes(action_results)` | Post-session learning loop (writes inferred outcomes for each action's trace) | takes the engine's tracker write lock | best-effort no-op (no `outcomes.resolve_pending`endpoint yet — follow-up) |

This lets callers pick the inference backend at runtime:

```
// In-process (offline dev, tests, CI)
let inference:  =
    new;
// Daemon-routed (`car-server` running locally; shared hot weights + accumulated profiles)
let inference:  =
    new;
```
`cmd_reason` in `car-cli` does the runtime selection — probes the daemon with a cheap `models.list` RPC and falls back to an embedded engine if unreachable. See `car-rs/crates/car-cli/src/daemon_handle.rs` for the daemon-side `ReasoningInferenceHandle` impl.

**Why a new trait instead of growing  InferenceHandle.**

`InferenceHandle` (added in #188 for memgine) is intentionally minimal — `generate` + `embed` — because memgine is reachable from many crates and a wide trait surface multiplies daemon-proxy work for every implementor. `ReasoningInferenceHandle` extends it with the three methods car-reason actually uses, keeping the lower-level trait clean while still letting daemon impls compose: `DaemonInferenceHandle` implements both, with one shared WebSocket connection.

---
